indicator: Debt relative to income (debt-to-revenue for governments)
scale_or_threshold: No fixed cutoff; risk rises with level. US ≈ 580-583% of revenue (100% of GDP); JPN 1376%; FRA 478%; DEU 340%; CHN 321%; GBR 256%. Grids use 500-700% as the high end; Dalio says it is not clear exactly what risky debt levels are.
Rising values lead investors to stop lending and sell; toy model shows ~216-217% of income in year 1, 342% in the spiral case, 247% with monetization.

indicator: Nominal interest rate relative to inflation and nominal income growth
scale_or_threshold: Single most important variable; i > g makes debt compound faster than income; i − g = +2% ≈ +50% debt/income over 20 years; US CBO gap ≈ −0.4% (3.45% vs 3.9%).

indicator: Debt and debt service relative to savings/reserves
scale_or_threshold: Large savings buffer the other three; consistent deficits with negative expected surplus make debt grow quickly relative to savings.

indicator: Net selling of debt assets, especially government debt
scale_or_threshold: A big red flag; appears as runs on banks and rising rates with weak economy and currency.

indicator: Borrowing used to pay debt service
scale_or_threshold: Large and rising = sure sign of approaching debt crisis; US borrows ~20% of income per year to pay interest.

indicator: Debt growth versus income growth over extended periods
scale_or_threshold: Significantly faster debt growth for e.g. three years, with high asset prices relative to cash-flow values, marks a bubble (bubble indicator input).

indicator: Type of monetary policy in use
scale_or_threshold: MP0 (linked/hard) → MP1 (fiat, rate-driven) → MP2 (monetization) → MP3 (coordinated fiscal-monetary) → big deleveraging → return to hard money; the regime reveals the cycle stage. US: MP0 1945-71, MP1 1971-2008, MP2 2008-2020.

indicator: Real and nominal interest rates and supply/demand for debt
scale_or_threshold: Watched to tell tightening-against-inflation from a buyers' strike; private demand failing shows as rates rising while economy and currency are weak, or central bank spending reserves/printing to buy debt.

indicator: Central bank net worth and cash flow
scale_or_threshold: Losses on bonds when rates rise are notable; big red flag only when net worth is very negative and printing is needed to cover negative cash flow (central bank going broke).
Very wide early in the cycle (earnings yields ~4x bond yields in late 1940s-early 1950s); narrow late.

indicator: Government debt and money supply relative to gold
scale_or_threshold: US: 7x and 1.3x in 1945 versus 37x and 6x now.
Very high debt + very large deficits + low savings + very high and fast-rising interest rates = very high risk of default or devaluation crisis.
Debt-to-income typically must fall ~50% ± 20%; own-currency crises restructured in 1-3 years.
US ≈ 12% (CBO baseline); grids span 0-30%; tax-cut extension adds 8% of revenue per year.

indicator: Share of debt maturing each year
scale_or_threshold: US ≈ 35%; shortening maturities under stress raise principal payments.

indicator: Money stock (M0) relative to government income
scale_or_threshold: US ≈ 110% ($5.7T); monetization scenario takes it to $11.8T over 10 years.

indicator: Private sector maximum willingness to hold government bonds (% of government income)
scale_or_threshold: Grid axis 700% down to 100%; at 600% cap with 600% starting debt the central bank must print 59% of government income over 10 years.
Expected FX move per 1%-of-GDP rise in M0 of 0.5-2.0%; 1.0% sensitivity with 600% cap implies ~−10% over 10 years, up to −89% at 2.0% sensitivity and 100% cap.
Monitored for rises and declines of great powers: indebtedness with weakening monetary systems; education, infrastructure, law and order, civility, government effectiveness.
